newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Negotiators seek to end Colombian truckers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Negotiators seek to end Colombian truckers' strike.

text.p: Colombian Interior Minister Horacio Serpa huddled with representatives of striking truck drivers Wednesday in a bid to end a 10-day work stoppage that has wreaked havoc with the economy.

There was no immediate word on the outcome of the talks, which also involved Transportation Minister Carlos Hernan Lopez and several other cabinet ministers, but truckers said they were hopeful about reaching a quick settlement of the strike that has paralyzed Colombia's export industries since it began at midnight October 13.

"We're the ones who are most interested in reaching a solution," said Alfredo Cuervo, a spokesmen for the Colombian Truck Drivers Association (ACC). The ACC, which represents about 90,000 drivers nationwide, called the strike to press for higher wages and lower taxes and tolls.
Local media reports early Wednesday said Lopez had ruled out any further negotiations with the truckers, whose work stoppage was declared illegal by the government last week.

But government sources said Serpa, an able negotiator and acting head of state since President Ernesto Samper departed on a whirlwind tour of Asia last Friday, had personally ordered the restart of negotiations Wednesday morning.
